newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Ralph wants accounting board scrapped.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Ralph wants accounting board scrapped.

text.p: Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD) president John Ralph on Thursday called for the local Accounting Standards Board to be scrapped and said U.S. accounting standards should be the norm here.
Ralph told reporters at the AICD's annual conference in Melbourne that many local companies already needed to conform to U.S. standards in order to raise capital in the United States.
"Personally I would favour disbanding the Accounting Standards Board in Australia and adopting U.S GAAP (generally accepted accounting principle) standards," he said.
Australian companies tapping the world's biggest capital market are asked to prepare two sets of annual accounts, one for the local market and another for the U.S. market, he said.
"The U.S. GAAP is regarded as being satisfactory for servicing the biggest economy in the world...why not use their accounting standards and produce one set of numbers," he added.
Ralph is chairman of Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and incoming chairman of industrial group Pacific Dunlop Ltd.
